_comment: Canonical invoke payloads for the script commands (spec §46.2).
Read by BOTH sides so the DTOs cannot drift apart again:
TypeScript wrappers in src/control/services/scripts.ts emit exactly
argument types deserialize exactly these payloads.
import_script and export_script carry NO filesystem path (spec §50.7).
Rust runs the native dialog and does the I/O in one trusted operation, so
the control webview cannot name a file to read or a file to truncate.
`suggestedName` only seeds the save dialog's default file name.
_list_scripts_comment: C3/C7/S2. The library's `view` is a UI concept with no field in Rust's
ScriptFilter; control used to send it anyway, serde dropped it, and the
Trash view listed the LIVE scripts. The view is mapped to status /
openedOnly here, `sort` uses the keys repo.rs matches on, and `page` is a
PageRequest struct — it was typed as a bare number on the TS side.
_revision_comment: Spec §21.4 revision browser. These three commands were implemented and
tested in Rust with no TypeScript caller at all, so every snapshot the
app took was write-only. Argument names are the camelCase forms of the
restore_revision is a compare-and-swap like any other save: it carries
the revision the editor believes it holds, and Rust snapshots the
preimage with reason `before_restore` before overwriting it.
_revision_reasons_comment: Every reason string Rust can write into script_revisions.reason. The UI
maps each to a label; the Rust test asserts repo.rs/import_export.rs
write no reason outside this list, so a new one cannot reach the panel
